65K likes, 197 comments - jeffnippard on October 11, 2026: "How important is the mind-muscle connection?

The “mind-muscle connection” is exactly what it sounds like: when you think about the muscle you’re trying to target as you lift.

Bodybuilders have been talking about it for decades, but does it actually matter?

Well, there is some research suggesting it can enhance growth. A 2018 study found significantly greater biceps growth when participants focused on “feeling the muscle” rather than simply moving the weight. However, the overall body of evidence is still quite limited, and the effect doesn’t seem to be huge.

I still use it sometimes in my own training though. For example, if I am trying to isolate my lats on a pulldown, I think about feeling my lats stretch and squeeze. This can help keep my mid-traps and rhomboids from taking over. I also think about using my side delts on lateral raises to prevent my traps or front delts from doing too much work.

I usually skip the mind-muscle connection on heavy compound lifts like squats, presses, rows and deadlifts though, and just focus on using good form.

Do you use the mind-muscle connection in your training?".

139K likes, 603 comments - jeffnippard on September 14, 2026: "I’m hitting my biceps and triceps every day for 30 days straight to see how much they’ll grow. This is my latest upper body workout for the case study, where I hit arms first to prioritize them further.

I’m getting ultrasound and circumference measurements each week to see exactly when the growth happens (if it does lol) and then doing a 2 week follow up after the 30 days to see if the growth was just pump/swelling or if I actually built new muscle tissue. I’m on day 16 of 30 now so once the case study is finished, the video with the final results will go up on YouTube soon after.

Do you think 30 days is enough time to see significant growth or nah?

Love this French press machine, 4 sets x 8-12 reps

Mostly doing flyes (as opposed to presses) for my pecs during the case study to better control for triceps volume

Isolating the lats/teres here because I’m not doing pull downs during the case study. I just don’t want any indirect bicep work to throw off the volume analytics ha

Kelso shrugs! Lately been going a bit lighter and focusing more on squeezing + mind muscle connection with my mid traps

3 sets x 10-12 lean away laterals for side delts

~20 rep cross body reverse pec deck lengthened partials for rear delts to finish".

273K likes, 1,103 comments - jeffnippard on August 20, 2026: "Caffeine is one of the few supplements that have actually been shown to give an immediate (but modest) strength boost. About 75-150 mg of caffeine for a 180 lb lifter seems to be enough. 

People were able to lift about 7 extra pounds on the squat when they took caffeine on the upper end of that dose range in a 2019 study. 

Going even higher (~400 to 570 mg) has been studied and it does seem to provide a larger effect in some cases, but it’s just not worth the increased risk of sleep disturbance in my opinion. Plus, Health Canada says you shouldn’t exceed 400 mg a day for health.

I’d say the best science-based advice is to take 1-2 mg of caffeine per kilogram of body weight about 30-60 minutes before training, but only on days when you really need it. If you always take caffeine before every workout, you’ll probably develop a tolerance and not get the same strength boost over time.

PMID references: 35203046, 31575825, 39170391".
